A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same POLAR study. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original MCTS analyses, benchmark evaluations of POLAR and baselines, and inference-latency measurements in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and latency results and explicitly reports rerunning the affected in-distribution analyses after correcting data preparation.

M1.justification: The segmentation representation, skip/keep/repeat operations, predictor architecture, training losses, and beam-search decoding in Section 3 are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same MCTS procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate DART-Math DM-1 through DM-5, ASDiv, MAWPS, and the same MMLU-Pro subjects. Deduplication changes sampling and splits within retained coverage, without adding a task or domain.

E2.justification: Matched tables retain the same comparator sets: greedy and sampling baselines, ShortGPT, MindSkip, FlexiDepth, and DR.LLM, plus the same MCTS operator variants. Figure 8 clarifies its Base label as sampling, consistent with the sampling comparison already discussed in v1's Section 4.2.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix D.1 introduce question-text deduplication before splitting. Total train/validation/test counts change from 6,250/1,250/2,500 to 4,130/826/1,651, retaining approximately the same proportions. The revision note explicitly confirms rerunning affected in-distribution analyses. Appendix D.2 also replaces fixed 10-step warmup with validation-tuned warmup.

E4.justification: The operator ablation in Table 1 and depth, recurrence, and program-structure analyses in Figures 3–7 receive revised empirical evidence following data cleaning. Their questions and analysis scope remain the same; no new ablation family, robustness scenario, or case study is introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the empirical comparisons. The rerun statement concerns the corrected dataset protocol, not additional statistical replication or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 5–7 and Figures 3–8 replace substantial in-distribution results. In Table 2, LLaMA DM-1 pass@5 Base/POLAR scores change from 47.6/68.4% to 65.2/74.5%. In Table 7, Qwen3 DM-1 pass@5 changes from FlexiDepth exceeding POLAR, 84.8 versus 55.6%, to POLAR exceeding FlexiDepth, 80.1 versus 55.3%. These are revised-setting results, not same-setting gains. OOD tables remain unchanged; Table 4 updates accuracy gains but retains latency values.

T1.justification: The program definitions, composition equations, segmentation constraints, prediction losses, and MCTS reward and UCB formulation are unchanged. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: discovering alternative layer programs, predicting them with a lightweight network, improving accuracy and efficiency, and transferring across domains. Revised evidence does not redefine these central claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.1 qualifies consistent superiority as generally outperforming baselines and stronger performance in most settings. Section 4.2 now explicitly limits the shorter-program interpretation to successful top-5 candidates and replaces the diminishing-returns discussion with a macro-averaged comparison. The broader mechanism explanations and applicability limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly identifies the MATH pool and documents deduplication and resulting counts. Figure 8 specifies macro-averaging and the shortest-successful-top-5 CDF. Conversely, Appendix D.2 removes the 50-token generation-limit disclosure and gives no warmup tuning range or selected value. The deletion does not establish an actual output-limit change.

R1.justification: The references, Section 5, and Appendix A retain the same cited works and positioning relative to early exit, layer skipping, recurrence, and DR.LLM.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites in Section 4.2 and Appendices C.1 and D explain the corrected evaluation and adjust its narrative. Most prose and the section and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 8 revises its axes and explanatory caption; captions for Tables 2 and 5–7 are shortened. Table 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, with accompanying text reflow. The figure and table inventory and overall visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: Deduplicating questions before splitting and rerunning the affected analyses addresses an important train/test question-overlap risk in the paper's central empirical evidence (Appendix D.1; Tables 1, 2, and 5–7). This substantially strengthens evaluation credibility independently of whether individual scores rise or fall. Clearer Figure 8 reporting also helps. Removing the generation-limit disclosure and leaving warmup tuning unspecified are smaller reproducibility losses.
